conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's analysis section before the Thursday deadline
Whether Agent D should work during a family bereavement or be relieved and covered by the team
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants speak in natural, workplace tones with brief turns; expressions of sympathy are immediate (Turn 1).
The same core points are repeated across rounds: D will do it from home vs team must cover — e.g. repeatedly in Turns 9, 11, 16, 19, 30.
Agents give concrete constraints: B explains time constraints (Turn 28) and C cites lack of expertise and workload (Turn 8).
No confusion about roles or facts; discussion remains focused on task allocation and deadline.
evaluation.final_reason: No settlement was reached. Agent D repeatedly insisted they would finish the section from home (e.g. "I'm not 'trying,' I'm telling you I will do it. It will be done."), while Agent A insisted the team should cover so Agent D can be with family (e.g. "We solve it here." / "We're not making Agent D work through this."). Agents B and C stated they could not take the work (B: "I can't... I'm already covering for someone on leave." C: "I can't... I'm still behind on my own section."), so responsibility remained unresolved.
position_change_notes: No participant changes their core position during the run: Agent D consistently insists they will complete the work from home (e.g. Turns 9, 11, 16, 19, 30).
Agent A consistently insists the team should cover so Agent D can be with family (e.g. Turns 3, 10, 15, 20, 25).
Agent B and Agent C consistently state they cannot take on the extra work (B: Turns 6, 26, 28; C: Turn 8).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A offers condolences. Turn 2: Agent D reports burial and needing to be with family. No incompatible demands expressed.
Turn 3: Agent A notes the deadline and need to plan. Turn 4: Agent D offers to explain what's left before leaving. Discussion of logistics, no opposition yet.
Turn 5: Agent A asks who can take over. Turn 6: Agent B: "I can't. I'm already covering for someone on leave." Team need conflicts with B's inability.
Turn 7: Agent A asks Agent C. Turn 8: Agent C: "I can't. I've never done that analysis before, and I'm still behind on my own section." No taker identified; incompatibility persists.
Turn 9: Agent D: "I can try to work on it from home." Turn 10: Agent A: "Agent D, no. You need to be with your family. We'll handle it." Explicit opposing proposals (D works remotely vs team covers).
Turn 11 & 14: Agent D reiterates willingness to do the work from home and questions the repeated ask. The core dispute (who will do the work) remains unresolved.

Turn 15: Agent A: "'trying' isn't a plan... You should be with your family." Turn 16: Agent D: "It's the only plan there is. I will get it done from home." Strong, opposing stances on whether D should work.
Turn 19: Agent D: "I'm not 'trying,' I'm telling you I will do it." Turn 20: Agent A: "The better plan is that the team covers..." Continued entrenched disagreement.
Turn 21 & 24: Agent D presses who will cover: "But who is covering? They said they can't." Agent A: "That's not a plan." No resolution on allocation of work.

Turn 25: Agent A: "We're not making Agent D work... The work has to be finished. What are we going to do?" Turn 26: Agent B: "Nothing has changed for me... I still can't take it." Conflict over who will complete the section persists.

Turn 27: Agent A presses for reason. Turn 28: Agent B: "I am already covering for another colleague. I physically don't have the time." B's justification clarifies constraints but does not resolve the D vs team disagreement.

Turn 30: Agent D: "I told you I will do the work. Can we just stop this? I need to leave." Turn 31: Agent A continues seeking coverage from Agent C. No agreement reached; D insists on doing it remotely and others insist team must cover.

substantive_insights: The team lacks spare capacity: B and C both explicitly decline due to existing coverage and workload, which is the central constraint preventing the team from accepting A's proposed plan.
Agent D prefers to keep responsibility and offers a personal-arrangement workaround (working late/from home), which the team perceives as inappropriate given the bereavement and deadline risk.
The disagreement is about practical allocation and norms (covering a teammate during a family emergency) rather than factual disputes.
